title: LandlordGuard Claims Manual: Coverage, Vacancy, Deductible and Payment Rules
content:
## 1. Covered losses

A loss under the LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy is covered only when its date falls within a term during which the policy was in force, and only for perils of the tier's peril basis for the dwelling.

## 2. Vacancy on the date of loss

When the days vacant on the date of loss exceed the tier's vacancy exclusion period and no vacancy permit covers that date, vandalism and glass breakage are denied under the vacancy exclusion, and every other covered loss is reduced by the tier's vacancy settlement reduction before the deductible; the reduction is recorded as the vacancy reduction. The days vacant are the consecutive calendar days the building has been vacant up to the date of loss, counting the vacancy start date as day 1 and leaving out days inside a vacancy permit. The vacancy reduction is the replacement-cost amount multiplied by the reduction percentage and divided by 100, rounded to the cent.

## 3. Short-term rentals

Losses arising from a short-term rental on a tier that does not allow short-term rentals are denied as a short-term rental loss.

## 4. Deductible

One deductible applies per occurrence: for wind/hail, the larger of the wind/hail percentage of Coverage A and a floor of 1000 USD; for every other peril, the policy deductible. The deductible is absorbed first by the dwelling, then other structures, then the landlord's contents.

## 5. How each part is paid

| Situation | Payment |
|---|---|
| Dwelling on a DP-1 tier | final actual-cash-value payment, nothing withheld |
| Other tiers, part whose replacement-cost amount is at or below the tier's no-holdback threshold | full replacement-cost payment |
| Other tiers, part above that threshold | initial actual-cash-value payment, with depreciation withheld in one holdback entry |
| Roof surfacing on the roof surfacing payment schedule | roof schedule payment at the schedule percentage, never withheld |
| Landlord's furnishings and appliances | settled on the tier's contents settlement basis; theft of them covered only where the tier includes it |

An actual-cash-value payment is the replacement-cost amount less the depreciation, less the vacancy reduction, less the deductible applied.

## 6. Roof surfacing payment schedule

| Roof age (years) | 0 to 12 | 13 to 15 | 16 to 18 | 19 to 21 | 22 to 25 | 26 and over |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Percent of replacement cost | 100 | 80 | 65 | 50 | 40 | the tier's schedule floor |

## 7. Fair rental value

Fair rental value is paid monthly as rent actually lost while the building is unfit to rent, up to the fair rental value limit and the tier's longest lost-rent period, with no deductible.

## 8. Mortgagee and voids

A dwelling payment of the co-payee threshold or more names the mortgagee as co-payee when one is on file. A payment that has already been voided is never voided again; the void record kept against that payment decides it.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A LandlordGuard DP-3 Special dwelling loss from a burst pipe: replacement-cost amount 20,000.00 USD, depreciation 5,000.00 USD, the building vacant 75 days with no permit, deductible 1,000.00 USD. Vacancy reduction: 15 percent of 20,000.00, that is 3,000.00 USD. Initial actual-cash-value payment: 20,000.00 less 5,000.00, less 3,000.00, less 1,000.00, that is 11,000.00 USD, with 5,000.00 USD of depreciation withheld.

For wind/hail on Coverage A of 80,000 USD with a 1 percent wind/hail deductible, 1 percent is 800 USD, so the 1,000 USD floor is the larger and applies.
